rationale: Twice in Genesis a master's household is said to be blessed by the LORD because of a descendant of Abraham who works in it: Jacob in his uncle Laban's household, and Joseph in the Egyptian Potiphar's. Laban says, 'I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you' (30:27, BSB), and Jacob answers, 'The LORD has blessed you wherever I set foot' (30:30). Of Joseph in Potiphar's house the narrator says, 'the LORD blessed the Egyptian's household on account of him' (39:5). The BSB's English differs ('because of you', 'on account of him'), but Bible Hub's interlinear shows the same Hebrew word, biglal (Strong's 1558), in both 30:27 and 39:5. The word alone is not distinctive: Bible Hub's concordance lists ten occurrences, three of them in Genesis (12:13, 30:27, 39:5), and the other Genesis use is Abram's 'on account of you my life will be spared' (12:13), which is not about blessing. The stronger evidence is the combination: the LORD as subject, the verb 'bless' and biglal together occur in Genesis only at 30:27 and 39:5. A named reader joins the two scenes, though through Jacob's reply rather than through biglal: Genesis Rabbah 73:8, commenting on 30:30 (where the Hebrew is leragli, literally 'at my foot'), says 'everywhere the righteous go, blessing is sent', and lists Isaac in Gerar (26:12), Jacob with Laban (30:30) and 'Joseph descended to Potiphar, blessing came on his account' (39:5). Graded motif at strong, following conn-gen24-gates-gen22, because the recurring collocation in a matching situation is checkable in the same book and a named reader links the scenes. It is not graded type_antitype or promise_fulfillment. Neither verse cites the promise to Abram that 'all the families of the earth will be blessed through you' (12:3). Barnes, on 39:5, ties the Joseph verse to that promise ('He blesses those who bless his own Genesis 12:3'), and the Cambridge Bible, on 30:30, points Jacob's 'increased' to 28:14 through the verb ('Heb. broken forth. See Genesis 28:14'). No source read for this lesson links 30:27 itself to 12:3, so no row from 30:27 to 12:3 is authored. The speaker in 30:27 is Laban, who says he learned it 'by divination'; the narrator of 39:5 states it in his own voice. That difference is part of what a reader weighs, and the row does not decide it.
